ctx.x: And of course, they all played the colleges - they'd be split up, you know, and I would be playing the colleges, too, the local bands, so I had a chance to hear these people in person. Nowadays, a boy goes to school, he goes to college, and he gets the charts, he gets Woody Herman's charts. But I had a chance to be there in person and watch these people. That was my musical training.

Among others, I saw Paul Whiteman's band, the Rythm Boys back in those days, and Bing Crosby, and Jack and Charlie Teagarden were in the band playing that old Archer Pier. And Roy Bargy, Bix Beiderbecke, the Casaloma Band started there about 1932 -- oh, that was a big band in those days, organized and became a very big thing.
So I had a chance to see these people in person.
